name: Up-diagonal turned dash climb: turned dashes from a cling slide up the wall and get the dash back
techNote: A Ground wall (right face x 0, top y 1600) over a floor, the finish box on its top. The start is inwall-wallbounce's cling on its face at y 95 (stick toward the wall). Dash with the stick at rest and push up and toward the wall in the dash freeze (turnX -1, turnY 1): from a cling the dash flips away from the wall (its first tick goes 13.4 u out), the freeze turn aims it back up-diagonally into the wall, and the wall turns it straight up at full dash speed (1670 u/s) while FixedUpdate's wall branch, open while dashActive (Movement.cs 1006), calls touchedSolidGround on the Ground-tagged face and gives the air dash back. It slides 266.4 u up and clings again with the dash in hand; two rest inputs later the next turned dash goes. Six dashes, 13 ticks apart, carry the dot over the top at 1600: finish on tick 91. No step-up is involved, so the climb doesn't depend on the frame rate. A dash pressed up or up-diagonal from the cling flips away from the wall instead, and without the wall jump unlock the wall branch is off: no refill, no turn upward, no cling.
